title: Mid-Think: Training-Free Intermediate-Budget Reasoning via Token-Level Triggers
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. The authors analyze existing reasoning datasets (OpenR1-Math-220k, OpenMathReasoning) and the outputs of DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3, showing all are dominated by traces beginning with 'Okay'/'Alright' after <think>, which is the source of the trigger-token 'overfitting.' For RL, they sample two 5,000-problem sets from Skywork-OR1-RL-Data (math, evaluated on AIME) and OpenScienceReasoning-2 (science, evaluated on GPQA); the compact size is intentional to limit reward hacking. Evaluation uses MATH500, AIME22-24, GPQA, and LiveCodeBench. No new data is generated; the contribution is identifying trigger patterns within existing SFT/RL data.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The pipeline is the standard base -> SFT -> RL(GRPO) ordering of Qwen3. Mid-Think is used at two points: as a training-free inference-time format, and as the rollout/training mode during the RL stage after SFT. RL trains Qwen3-4B/8B with GRPO for 6 epochs (lr 1e-6, 8 responses/prompt, 16K max tokens, 8xH200). Three modes (Think, No-Think, Mid-Think) share identical hyperparameters for fair comparison. There is no multi-stage RL or self-play; the novelty is substituting the Mid-Think prompt format as the RL objective to raise entropy and shorten rollouts.
method:
Mid-Think is a training-free prompting format built on the discovery that hybrid-thinking models' reasoning is governed by a few trigger tokens, not high-level instructions. Attention analysis on Qwen3-8B shows the 'Okay' token after <think> activates reasoning (3.18x attention ratio) while the 

 after </think> suppresses it (5.27x). Mid-Think combines both: the format <think>

</think>

<reason>
Okay... simultaneously activates both trigger regions, inducing intermediate-budget reasoning at roughly a 0.5 budget. The <reason> tag is replaceable (<begin>, <less think>). The trigger is template-derived: DASD-4B-Thinking (trained on 'We need' traces) shifts the trigger to 'We', and a mismatched trigger collapses to No-Think. Beyond inference, Mid-Think serves as the GRPO rollout/training mode after SFT, raising policy entropy and shortening outputs to cut training time ~15% while improving accuracy. Versus fixed-token and prompt-based budget baselines it gives finer-grained, Pareto-optimal control.
eval_metrics: Benchmarks: MATH500, AIME22-24, GPQA, and LiveCodeBench. Metrics: accuracy, average generation length, wait count (occurrences of 'wait'-like tokens), training entropy, and training time. Models span hybrid-think (Qwen3-4B/8B/14B/32B, Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE), pure-think (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, -Llama-8B, Phi-4-mini-reasoning), and DASD-4B-Thinking. A budget-controlled baseline (truncating Think traces to 0.1-1.0 of tokens) builds an accuracy-length Pareto curve; Mid-Think sits near a 0.5 budget and surpasses the frontier on GPQA. RL uses GRPO via verl on 8xH200. Headline: Qwen3-8B Mid-Think RL (Think-test) lifts AIME 69.8%->72.4%, GPQA 58.5%->61.1%, MATH500 92.4%->94.1%, training time 54h->46h. Training-free Qwen3-8B MATH500: No-Think 83.2%/899 tok, Mid-Think 92.3%/2589, Think 94.6%/4904; LiveCodeBench Qwen3-8B No-T 40.8% / Mid-T 49.7% / Think 65.9%.
key_results: Qwen3-8B trained with Mid-Think as the GRPO objective improves Think-test AIME 69.8%->72.4% and GPQA 58.5%->61.1% while cutting RL training time ~15% (54h->46h). Training-free Mid-Think on MATH500 (Qwen3-8B) reaches 92.3% accuracy at 2,589 tokens versus 94.6%/4,904 for Think and 83.2%/899 for No-Think, and on LiveCodeBench Qwen3-8B improves No-Think 40.8%->49.7% (Mid-Think).
evolution_note: Builds on the attention-sink / token-cue line (No-Wait, SpecExit, Speculative Thinking) and on hybrid-thinking models (Qwen3, Gemini, GPT-oss, DeepSeek V3.1) by reframing Think/No-Think switching as overfitting to a few trigger tokens inherited from SFT data templates. In the 2026 RLVR/GRPO era it offers a lightweight, training-free route to intermediate reasoning budgets and motivates template-aware budget control for cheaper, higher-entropy RL training.
